sections.title: Executive summary
lines: 1000 network records were analysed. 183 were classified as Normal and 817 as Malicious. The uploaded data received a quality score of 100/100 (Grade A). 1 records require Review; 0 were rejected.
Current-upload findings below are separate from saved official model evaluation.

sections.title: Model Performance - Official Test Evaluation

UNSW-NB15 reserved official testing split; 82332 evaluated records
Accuracy: 86.4%; Precision: 80.7%; Recall: 99%; F1-score: 88.9%

False positives are normal traffic classified as malicious. False negatives are missed malicious traffic.

sections.title: Reliability - predictive-input integrity
lines: High: 999; Review: 1; Low: 0; Rejected: 0 (included in Low).
High: prediction produced with no unresolved predictive-input integrity issue.
Review: prediction produced, but input had a relevant handled quality issue.
Low: prediction could not be safely produced due to invalid required input; rejected records have no class or probability.
Reliability describes input integrity, separate from model probability; it is not guaranteed correctness.

sections.title: Security recommendations
lines: Backend decision-support recommendations for human review and investigation.
high priority: Prioritise human review of malicious predictions with input-integrity issues.
Reason: Malicious predictions requiring Review: 1. Input issues may affect interpretation.
Affected records: 1
high priority: Investigate model-predicted malicious records using independent security evidence.
Reason: 817 records were predicted Malicious. A probability estimate does not establish a confirmed attack.
Affected records: 817
medium priority: Preserve analytical anomalies for contextual security investigation.
Reason: 706 distinct records have analytical findings; these are not automatically bad input or confirmed attacks.
Affected records: 706

sections.title: Limitations
lines: Model probabilities are estimates, not calibrated guarantees. Input reliability is not guaranteed prediction correctness.
Analytical anomalies are not automatically attacks. The model requires compatible network features.
This prototype analyses uploaded network records, not live packet capture.
Only the currently returned record window is available for selection. The PDF does not include all predictions, evidence arrays, anomaly occurrences or raw audit structures.
Official evaluation is saved Phase 5 performance; model selection used that testing split, so it is not a fresh independent evaluation of the selected winner.
Analysis date/time is not supplied by the current backend response; no analysis timestamp was inferred.

source: Real frontend/backend upload; first 1000 testing rows; 100 returned records
